title: Digital Painting 101 — Full Free Course
author: Matt Kohr (Ctrl+Paint)
note: THE starting point. Structured like a real course. Free. Do this before anything else if you haven't.

title: Perspective Made Easy — Drawabox
author: Uncomfortable (Drawabox)
note: Free, rigorous perspective and construction fundamentals. Does the structural thinking that unlocks environments and props.

title: Figure Drawing for All It's Worth — Free Lessons
author: Stan Prokopenko (Proko)
note: Best free anatomy channel. Start with the Bean and Mannequinization series. Directly relevant to character design.

title: 10 Minutes to Better Painting — Color Series
author: Marco Bucci
note: Compact, dense color theory lessons. His 'How I Paint' series shows a full real-time process. Essential.

title: Painting with Light and Color
author: James Gurney (Gurney Journey)
note: Free blog from the Dinotopia artist. Deep posts on color temperature, light physics, and plein air observation. High signal.

title: Concept Art Fundamentals — FZD School
author: Feng Zhu
note: Feng Zhu ran one of the world's top concept art schools. His free YouTube lectures cover design language, ideation, and industry expectations.

title: Environment Concept Art — Full Breakdown
author: Tyler Edlin
note: Tyler works in games and films. His process videos show how to go from thumbnail to polished environment concept. Very relevant to your goals.

title: Paint Like a Beginner — Process Series
author: Sinix Design
note: One of the most concise digital painting teachers. His 'Everything You Need to Know' video alone is worth an hour.

title: Character Design — Full Process
author: Ahmed Aldoori
note: Clean, methodical character design breakdowns. Strong on silhouette, shape language, and industry-standard presentation.

title: Dynamic Sketching — Foundations
author: Peter Han
note: Peter Han's mark-making and organic form approach is foundational for concept artists. Makes your sketchbook work translate to digital.

title: Composition and Visual Design
author: Will Weston
note: Free blog posts on composition principles used in film and games. Particularly good on visual hierarchy and eye flow.

title: How to Paint — Free Sample Lessons
author: NMA (New Masters Academy)
note: Atelier-level instruction. Free YouTube content includes anatomy, cast drawing, and figure painting demos.

title: Realistic Ink & Sketching Techniques
author: Karl Kopinski
note: Karl's ink-first approach is excellent for building a strong sketchbook practice. His gestural speed is inspiring and learnable.

title: Concept Art Career Advice
author: Robotpencil (Justin Cherry)
note: Practical advice on portfolio building, getting into studios, and the realities of concept art work. Very honest, very useful.

title: Visual Storytelling for Games and Film
author: CGMA Art School
note: CGMA runs paid courses but their YouTube channel has high-quality free demo content from working industry professionals.

title: Bobby Chiu — Character Design Masterclass
author: Bobby Chiu (Imaginism Studios)
note: Bobby's whimsical characters show strong narrative design. His interviews with industry artists are also worth studying.

title: Line of Action — Free Timed Drawing Practice
author: Line of Action
note: Free timed pose reference tool. Use for daily warm-ups. Set to 30-second or 1-minute gestures to build speed and confidence.

title: Watts Atelier — Free YouTube Lessons
author: Jeff Watts
note: Traditional atelier training adapted for working artists. Strong on head drawing and figure which carries into portrait concept work.

title: Visual Development — Schoolism Free Content
author: Schoolism
note: Schoolism has some of the best instructors in the industry (Bobby Chiu, Nathan Fowkes). Free YouTube content is a preview of their paid courses.

title: Pixel Art for Games — Brandon James Greer
author: Brandon James Greer
note: Relevant if working on game sprites or emotes. His tutorials cover animation, colour palettes, and game-ready assets.

title: Splash Art Breakdown — League of Legends
author: Various Riot Artists (ArtStation)
note: Study Riot splash art breakdowns on ArtStation. Note the lighting, character readability, and background integration. This is your long-term target.

title: Colour and Light — Full Free Reference
author: James Gurney
note: Get this book. It's the industry standard reference. Not free but ~£20 and worth every penny. Look for PDFs online in the meantime.

title: How to Make Emotes for Twitch/Discord
author: Various Game Artists (YouTube)
note: Directly relevant to your emote commission. Key points: 112x112px minimum, strong silhouette, bold colours, readable at tiny sizes.

title: Game Prop Design Fundamentals
author: Tyler Edlin + FZD blend
note: For your chess piece commission — props need a clear read at multiple scales. Study how game props communicate faction/function through silhouette.
